meta.description: The survey S1 of (14): 22 speakers read aloud lists of -able adjectives, among them those on remedy and parody, treating them as nonce forms. The table counts the responses with each stress pattern relative to the verb; some speakers gave more than one pronunciation, so the remedy responses number 24.

types.name: Base
types.doc: The verb the -able adjective is formed on.

levels.name: remedy
levels.label: rémedy
levels.doc: remedy, whose paradigm lists the amphibrachic stem of remedial

levels.name: parody
levels.label: párody
levels.doc: parody, whose paradigm lists only the dactylic verb

types.name: Pattern
types.doc: The stress pattern of the stem of the -able form, relative to the verb.

levels.name: sameAsBase
levels.label: σ́σσ
levels.doc: same as the verb, stress on the first syllable

levels.name: second
levels.label: σσ́σ
levels.doc: stress shifted to the second syllable

levels.name: firstThird
levels.label: σ̀σσ́
levels.doc: stress on the first and third syllables

constants.name: speakers
constants.doc: The number of speakers surveyed in 1996-1997.

tables.name: responses
tables.doc: the responses with a stress pattern, of all responses to the -able form on a verb.

columns.name: total
columns.doc: All responses to the verb's -able form.
